ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two chemical species separated from each other, and with several curved arrows; the problem requires ignoring the arrows. The species on the left is shown as Ph2S bearing a positive charge, and connected through an S–O bond to a tert-butoxy fragment, namely Ph2S+–O–tBu. The species on the right is shown as a negatively charged alkoxide, written as −OC(CF3)2Ph. Reasoning: Expand the left cation Ph2S+–O–tBu as SMILES: CC(C)(C)O[S+](c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1. Expand the right anion −OC(CF3)2Ph as SMILES: [O-]C(c1ccccc1)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F. The two species are unconnected fragments, so connect them with a period.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as two separate species and ignore all reaction arrows. Convert the left cation by expanding Ph2S+–O–tBu into CC(C)(C)O[S+](c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.
